A big thank you to the lovely receptionists who were beyond patient and more than helpful! This also goes to RN Armani and doctor Keefe, who were super wonderful, helpful, and handled my kitty with such care and affection ♥️ thank you Small Door! 🤗

I just took my 2.5 month old Cavapoo puppy for his first appointment at Small Door West Village and was so delighted with the entire team.

Dr O’Callaghan and Nurse Erica made him feel super comfortable in his environment, giving toys and treats. Once he was settled, he took to the checkup and vaccines with no complaint or issue (he was very distracted by EasyCheese).

Dr O’Callaghan gave great tips and advice for taking care of a puppy in a big city as well as setting up a health plan.

I never thought I would have a puppy who would be excited to go to the vet, but here we are!

A couple of weeks ago, I took my 14-year-old cat to this veterinary practice because it was the only clinic with same-day availability. He was diagnosed with an upper respiratory infection and initially seemed to improve after receiving an injection. We spent nearly $800 during that first visit.
During the appointment, the veterinarian strongly recommended an additional X-ray, which was quoted at approximately $1,000. We were told it would be beneficial, but after seeking a second opinion from another veterinarian, we were advised that the imaging was not necessary at that time, so we decided to postpone it.
The following week, my cat’s condition worsened, so we returned to the same practice since I had already paid for their membership plan. Additional tests were performed, but we were told it would take several days for the results. Although my cat had not eaten for two days, the only medication prescribed was an ear ointment intended to stimulate his appetite.
The next day, after consulting with another veterinarian we know in PA, we learned there were 2 medications that should have been started immediately. We called this practice’s emergency number twice, left voicemail messages, and also emailed requesting the medications. We were told the veterinarian was not comfortable prescribing them without the pending test results.
At that point, our cat was critically ill. Thankfully, the veterinarian in PA prescribed the medications immediately and followed up the next day by adding a 3rd medication. We are grateful to Mixlab pet pharmacy on 37th St. for quickly preparing and dispensing the medications. Those medications saved our cat’s life, and today he is doing wonderfully.
This experience was heartbreaking. In our case, we felt that additional diagnostics took priority over providing timely treatment to a critically ill pet. We are incredibly grateful we sought a second opinion, and based on our experience, we will be choosing an independent veterinary practice rather than a large corporate chain for our pets going forward.
Our beloved cat is alive today because another veterinarian acted quickly when time mattered most.
